working_title: Common decline, divergent collapse: breeding-colony network structure predicts local resilience across Antarctic penguin islands
one_sentence_claim: Across neighboring Antarctic breeding islands, Adelie populations share an exceptionally strong long-term decline but differ in annual dynamics and extinction; simple climate/weather formulations fail prospective tests, while breeder distribution among subcolonies carries modest next-year information and independent Torgersen mapping confirms real habitat-structured sub-colony attrition.
new_evidence_role: external Torgersen mapping is phenomenon-level spatial triangulation only; colony-ID crosswalk remains unresolved
figure_plan: Figure 1: Palmer breeding-patch map and assembly endpoints
Figure 2: complete 1991-2017 five-island Adelie trajectories and annual synchrony
Figure 3: prospective mechanism audit using direction and relative held-out error change
Figure 4: conditional effective-colony signal, colony-network trajectories and Torgersen spatial attrition annotation
terminal_development_rule: No new climate window, weather month, colony-size threshold or topology index for the core paper. New core work is limited to figure/reproducibility/manuscript packaging or resolution of an external colony-code-to-polygon crosswalk.
